response:
Reflection: the frontier has stabilized and gen 6 was largely eliminative, which is informative. The peak remains dual cheapness (earnings yield plus net-capacity-to-price) with a two-year average of the capex-rate deviation from its own five-year norm (alpha 4.6%, t 4.82, Sharpe 0.544). Gen 6 ruled out four plausible extensions: the strictly-past norm does not survive smoothing (its gain and the smoothing gain overlap), three-year smoothing decays, a third revenue-based cheapness channel dilutes, gross plant is worse than net plant in the valuation leg, and the absolute maintenance benchmark carries no alpha at all — so the discipline signal is genuinely about *departure from the firm's own established policy*, not about the level of spending relative to physical replacement needs. With two generations left, this batch keeps the proven skeleton fixed and tests the few remaining first-order choices: how the deviation is scaled (proportional versus absolute), whether it should be purged of the industry capital cycle, whether horizon blending adds robustness, and — on the valuation side — whether the second cheapness channel works because it is asset-based, book-based, leverage-aware, or cash-adjusted.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Dual cheapness blended horizon deviation
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ppent, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), SUMRANK(NEG(SUB(RATIO(capx, ppegt), MA(RATIO(capx, ppegt), 5))), NEG(MA(SUB(RATIO(capx, ppegt), MA(RATIO(capx, ppegt), 5)), 2))))
HYPOTHESIS: The current-year deviation carries fresh information about a newly changed capital stance while the two-year average certifies durability; averaging their ranks should retain the responsiveness of the former and the reliability of the latter.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The unsmoothed deviation gave the highest FMB slope (6.85) and the smoothed one the highest alpha t-statistic (4.82), a pattern consistent with the two measuring the same regime at different signal-to-noise trade-offs. Blending them inside the discipline half keeps the valuation-discipline weighting at one half each, so any gain is attributable purely to horizon diversification.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Dual cheapness proportional capex deviation
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ppent, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), NEG(MA(LOG(RATIO(RATIO(capx, ppegt), MA(RATIO(capx, ppegt), 5))), 2)))
HYPOTHESIS: Discipline should be judged in proportional terms: a firm cutting its spending rate by a third is making the same allocation decision whether its normal rate is 6% or 20% of gross plant, but an absolute deviation mechanically assigns larger scores to capital-intensive firms.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every version of the winning leg used an absolute difference, so the cross-section of the discipline score is partly a cross-section of capital intensity, which is exactly the dimension FF5's investment factor already prices. A log ratio of current rate to own norm removes that scale dependence while preserving the own-benchmark economics, and should sharpen the peer comparison inside the sort.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Dual cheapness with peer-purged persistent deviation
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ppent, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(MA(SUB(RATIO(capx, ppegt), MA(RATIO(capx, ppegt), 5)), 2))))
HYPOTHESIS: Sustained retrenchment is only evidence of managerial discipline if peers are not retrenching simultaneously; demeaning the two-year deviation within industry isolates the firm-specific allocation choice from the common capital cycle.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Industry demeaning of the unsmoothed deviation held its own (alpha 4.3%), but it has never been combined with the persistence smoothing that produced the archive's most reliable alpha, and the two corrections address orthogonal contaminations — cross-sectional cycle versus single-year lumpiness. If both are needed, this becomes the cleanest statement of the mechanism.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Book and earnings cheapness with persistent restraint
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), NEG(MA(SUB(RATIO(capx, ppegt), MA(RATIO(capx, ppegt), 5)), 2)))
HYPOTHESIS: If the second cheapness channel helps because it anchors price to a balance-sheet stock rather than to a flow, then book equity per dollar of price should work at least as well as physical capacity per dollar of price, since it covers asset-light firms too.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is the decisive diagnostic on why dual cheapness improved the signal: capacity-to-price is both a stock anchor and a physical-asset anchor, and only substituting book equity separates the two explanations. A weaker result would confirm the physical-capacity interpretation and justify keeping ppent in the final signal despite its narrower economic reach; a stronger one would raise coverage and generality.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Cash-adjusted cheapness with persistent restraint
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ib, SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ppent, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), NEG(MA(SUB(RATIO(capx, ppegt), MA(RATIO(capx, ppegt), 5)), 2)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that stop investing accumulate cash, which inflates market capitalization without adding operating earnings and therefore makes disciplined allocators look artificially expensive; netting cash out of the price denominator removes this mechanical bias precisely where the interaction is supposed to bite.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is an economically motivated correction to a specific interaction-induced measurement error rather than a generic multiple swap, and it should matter most in the long leg where cash-rich retrenchers concentrate. It also revisits the enterprise-value idea that failed in early generations, but now attached to the discipline leg that actually works.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Operating cheapness with persistent restraint
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ppent, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), NEG(MA(SUB(RATIO(capx, ppegt), MA(RATIO(capx, ppegt), 5)), 2)))
HYPOTHESIS: Capital-allocation discipline is a whole-firm decision funded by debt as well as equity, so cheapness should be measured on enterprise value; a levered firm with a high EBITDA yield that is also spending below its own norm is deleveraging rather than empire building.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The EBITDA-to-enterprise-value leg produced respectable cross-sectional slopes in generations 0 and 1 but was always paired with a raw external-finance or acquisition leg that carried no alpha, so its portfolio value has never been fairly assessed. Pairing it with the proven persistent-deviation leg tests whether leverage-aware cheapness adds to, or merely duplicates, equity-based earnings yield.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
